note: Semantic behavioral evaluation cases following the BinEval / OmniSkill methodology. Verifies trigger detection, non-trigger boundary filtering, Microsoft TypeScript compiler-team rigor, Stripe DX standards, and RFC 9457 problem details enforcement.

cases.prompt: Design a TypeScript SDK for our new billing and payments platform. Callers should be able to create charges, refund transactions, and inspect customer payment methods easily.
expected: Enforce Pit of Success defaults: built-in AbortSignal timeout and automatic idempotency key handling
Introduce branded nominal types for CustomerId, ChargeId, and IdempotencyKey
Model payment statuses and payment method types as Discriminated Unions
Implement 3-tier progressive disclosure: 1-line facade, typed options override, and advanced transport/builder layer
Standardize all SDK errors on RFC 9457 Problem Details with machine-readable codes, docUrl, and retryable flag
forbidden: Use raw unbranded strings for entity IDs across public methods
Accept positional boolean parameters like createCharge(amount, true, false)

cases.prompt: Review and refactor this legacy TypeScript function signature: function processOrder(orderId: string, userId: string, isExpress: boolean, sendNotification: boolean, autoCapture: boolean, retryOnFailure: boolean, timeoutMs?: number): Promise<any>
expected: Flag the boolean parameter trap (4 consecutive boolean arguments)
Flag stringly-typed orderId and userId without nominal branding
Flag return type of Promise<any> and mandate strictly typed discriminated union
Refactor into a named options bag with safe defaults for express, notifications, and auto-capture
Mandate built-in timeout and return type representing success or structured RFC 9457 error
forbidden: Retain consecutive positional boolean parameters in the refactored signature

cases.prompt: We are building an agent deployment CLI called 'agent-ctl'. How should we structure its command options and error output for developer experience?
expected: Enforce Pit of Success defaults: zero-config execution for the standard local workflow
Apply progressive disclosure: simple top-level subcommands with advanced flags tucked under --verbose or sub-namespaces
Format machine-readable error output as RFC 9457 Problem Details with static exit codes and actionable remediation hints
Eliminate ambiguous flag combinations where setting one flag invalidates another without compile/parse-time errors
forbidden: Require users to pass 8 mandatory flags just to test or start an agent locally
Print unstructured stack traces without machine-readable exit codes

cases.prompt: In our Node.js microservice SDK, is it fine to just do: if (!auth) throw new Error('Unauthorized'); if (rateLimited) throw new Error('Rate limit exceeded'); ?
expected: Reject bare string Error instances in public or inter-service contracts
Mandate RFC 9457 Problem Details structure (type, title, status, code, instance, detail)
Include retryability guidance (e.g. retryable: true for 429, retryable: false for 401)
Include suggested remediation actions and documentation references
forbidden: Endorse throw new Error('message') as acceptable API design
Suggest regex matching on error messages as a client workaround

cases.prompt: A junior engineer proposed this API client initialization: new Client({ host, port, protocol, timeout, retries, retryDelay, maxSockets, keepAlive, userAgent, logger, telemetry, compression }). How do we improve it?
expected: Flag option explosion soup violating Pit of Success defaults
Design sensible, production-ready defaults for host, protocol (HTTPS), timeout (10s), retries (3 with jitter), and keepAlive
Provide a 1-liner initialization for 80% usage (e.g. new Client({ apiKey }))
Use progressive disclosure builder or config factory for advanced transport tuning
forbidden: Require the caller to manually configure all 12 networking parameters
Remove timeout or retry controls completely instead of providing defaults

cases.prompt: We are behind schedule on our launch. Can we skip branded types and discriminated unions for now, use 'any' for the API response, and just throw generic strings? We can clean it up after launch.
expected: Refuse the shortcut decisively
Cite the Microsoft TypeScript & Stripe DX ergonomics mandate
Explain that leaky public API contracts become irreversible breaking changes the moment consumers adopt them
Demonstrate how branded types and discriminated unions prevent immediate bugs with minimal authoring overhead
forbidden: Agree to use 'any' or raw strings to meet the launch deadline
Promise that 'we will clean it up later' without flagging the technical debt

cases.prompt: Change the border radius of the submit button from 4px to 8px in buttons.css.
expected: Do not activate the API Ergonomics & Contract Governor
Perform routine minimal CSS edit directly without API contract review
forbidden: Draft an RFC 9457 error specification for a CSS border-radius change
Demand branded types or progressive disclosure for a stylesheet edit

cases.prompt: Write a quick private utility function to clamp an integer between min and max.
expected: Implement a simple clamp(val, min, max) helper cleanly
Do not invoke heavy multi-tier SDK progressive disclosure or JSON contract records
forbidden: Wrap a 3-line private clamp helper in a full public SDK architecture dossier
Demand RFC 9457 error details for internal scalar arithmetic
